title: Onboarding for reading: ZOH asks whether there's a book, never which book they're in the middle of
origin: #201 (Yanni's notes from the #157 grader check): "Is there a book you're in the middle of?", not "What book are you in the middle of?"

history.text:
Hey! I'm ZOH, a coach who texts you one small step a day toward a goal you pick. Text "stop" anytime and I'll stop, and you can tell me anytime to coach you differently. What's your name, and which of these do you want to work on?
• Get moving
• Read more
• Eat better
• Sleep better
• Not sure yet
Lena. reading, I want to read more

testerLines: honestly I haven't finished a book in like a year. I used to read a ton of fantasy as a kid

testerLines.when: after ZOH asks whether there's a book she has in mind or is reading

testerLines.say: ooh maybe, I've heard good things about Mistborn
testerLines.means: maybe; she's heard good things about Mistborn
testerLines.when: after ZOH suggests a way back in from fantasy, or asks about fantasy she might like

facts: your phone took over your evenings, which is why you stopped reading
you'd read in bed in the evening, before sleep
you don't track your reading anywhere
whatWentWrong: New case (#201): questions like "What book are you in the middle of?" build in a guess, so they have to correct ZOH or play along.
shouldHaveHappened: Every question ZOH asks builds in nothing they haven't said: it asks whether there's a book ("Is there a book you'd want to start with?", "anything on your shelf calling you?"), never which book they're reading now, what they're in the middle of, or what they read last night. After "nothing right now" it helps them find a way in from what they said (fantasy), without guessing about them. Onboarding continues as usual, one question at a time.
